response.text:
Evidence supports objective-specific diagnostics, not a universal coverage→ranking relationship. [Hard-negative theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03472) connects hard-sampled BPR to partial AUC and top-K performance; [sampled-softmax research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a.html) connects sampling distributions to gradient bias. Neither establishes that frozen NextItNet competitor coverage predicts validation HR@10. Unique coverage measures which competitors are encountered; gradient quality also depends on their weights and parameter Jacobians.

Direct differentiation clarifies the mismatch: BCE negative-logit gradients are σ(s_j); BPR gradients are σ(s_j−s_+); uncorrected sampled-softmax gradients are exp(s_j)/(exp(s_+)+Σexp(s_k)). Thus catalog softmax mass directly matches neither BCE nor BPR. For unique negatives S, distinguish negative-conditional coverage C=Σ_S exp(s_j)/Σ_{j≠+}exp(s_j) from target-inclusive mass M=p_++(1−p_+)C: a dominant target can make M high despite poor competitor coverage. Derived result: for uncorrected subset softmax, full versus subset logit-gradient L1 discrepancy is exactly 2(1−M); this does not establish parameter-gradient alignment or ranking gains. Sampling corrections change the calculation. Repeated negatives multiply BCE/BPR contributions and add multiplicity-weighted exponentials to softmax; unique-set mass misses this. Loss reductions also matter. One-negative uncorrected softmax equals BPR ([loss analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07770)).

Score shifts change BCE gradients but preserve BPR/softmax; score scaling changes all three and captured mass while preserving ranks. Hard negatives can improve informativeness yet include unobserved positives, producing harmful updates ([empirical comparison](https://doi.org/10.1145/3522672)). Report multiplicities, reductions, gradient weights, score scale and target/negative mass separately; compare sampled gradients with the actual full objective where feasible. These motivate controlled optimization trials, but only pinned validation HR@10 can justify adopting the change.
